    // x = (R-r)cos t + r cos((R-r)/r t); y = (R-r)sin t - r sin((R-r)/r t).
    // Written component-wise because the two terms differ in sign.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypocycloid
    Eval(self: Hypocycloid2D, t: Number): Point2D
        => ((self.FixedRadius - self.RollingRadius) * t.Turns.Cos
                   + self.RollingRadius
                     * ((self.FixedRadius - self.RollingRadius) / self.RollingRadius
                        * t.Turns).Cos,
                   (self.FixedRadius - self.RollingRadius) * t.Turns.Sin
                   - self.RollingRadius
                     * ((self.FixedRadius - self.RollingRadius) / self.RollingRadius
                        * t.Turns).Sin);

    // x = (R+r)cos t - d cos((R+r)/r t); y = (R+r)sin t - d sin((R+r)/r t).
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epitrochoid
    Eval(self: Epitrochoid2D, t: Number): Point2D
        => (t.Turns.CirclePoint(self.FixedRadius + self.RollingRadius)
            - ((self.FixedRadius + self.RollingRadius) / self.RollingRadius * t.Turns)
                  .CirclePoint(self.PoleDistance))
           .ToPoint;

    // x = (R-r)cos t + d cos((R-r)/r t); y = (R-r)sin t - d sin((R-r)/r t).
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypotrochoid
    Eval(self: Hypotrochoid2D, t: Number): Point2D
        => ((self.FixedRadius - self.RollingRadius) * t.Turns.Cos
                   + self.PoleDistance
                     * ((self.FixedRadius - self.RollingRadius) / self.RollingRadius
                        * t.Turns).Cos,
                   (self.FixedRadius - self.RollingRadius) * t.Turns.Sin
                   - self.PoleDistance
                     * ((self.FixedRadius - self.RollingRadius) / self.RollingRadius
                        * t.Turns).Sin);

    //==
    // # Clothoid2D — the Euler spiral
    //
    // Curvature grows linearly with arc length, kappa(s) = s / Flatness^2, so
    // the tangent angle is theta(s) = s^2 / (2 Flatness^2) and the position is
    // the pair of Fresnel integrals of that angle. Those integrals have no
    // elementary closed form, so this is composite Simpson quadrature from the
    // origin to the requested arc length — the same thing a table lookup
    // interpolates, computed instead.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euler_spiral

    // The number of quadrature panels. Even, as Simpson requires; 64 holds the
    // error near machine precision over the arc lengths a transition curve uses
    // (the integrand oscillates faster as |s| grows, so a very long arc wants
    // more).
    QuadraturePanels(self: Clothoid2D): Integer => 64;

    // The tangent angle at signed arc length s.
    TangentAngleAt(self: Clothoid2D, s: Number): Angle
        => Angle(s * s / (2.0 * self.Flatness * self.Flatness));

    // Simpson's weight for sample i of n panels: 1 at the ends, 4 at odd
    // interior samples, 2 at even ones.
    SimpsonWeight(i: Integer, panels: Integer): Number
        => i == 0 || i == panels ? 1.0 : (i % 2 == 1 ? 4.0 : 2.0);

    // The point at the given unit parameter: the Fresnel integrals evaluated to
    // the arc length that parameter names within Domain.
    Eval(self: Clothoid2D, t: Number): Point2D {
        var panels = self.QuadraturePanels;
        var s = self.Domain.Lerp(t.Clamp(0.0, 1.0));
        var step = s / panels.ToNumber;
        var samples = (panels + 1).Range;
        var x = samples.Reduce(0.0, (acc, i) =>
            acc + SimpsonWeight(i, panels) * self.TangentAngleAt(step * i.ToNumber).Cos);
        var y = samples.Reduce(0.0, (acc, i) =>
            acc + SimpsonWeight(i, panels) * self.TangentAngleAt(step * i.ToNumber).Sin);
        return (x * step / 3.0, y * step / 3.0);
    }

    //==
    // # Evaluating the named space curves
    //
    // Closed-form evaluation of the space curves declared in `curves-shapes.types.plato`.
    //
    // Conventions:
    //   * The canonical curve parameter is `t` in [0, 1].
    //   * Types carrying an `Angles: AngleInterval` sweep map t through
    //     `Angles.Lerp(t)`; the knots and closed curves map t to `t.Turns`, one
    //     full revolution of their defining parameter.
    //   * Every formula is written in the curve's own frame and placed with
    //     `FramePoint` below, so the declaration comment "winds about the frame's
    //     Z axis" is what the body actually does.
    //
    // TODO(interface-gap): an angular curve whose natural parameter is an `Angle`,
    // bridged by one `Eval(curve, t: Number) => curve.Eval(t.Turns)`, has no
    // counterpart interface here. This is NOT a fold gap; the P2
    // `Reduce`/`MapRange` primitives do not touch it. The clean fix is a
    // `interface IAngularCurve3D` (obligation `Eval(self, theta: Angle): Point3D`)
    // plus one bridge, whose natural home is `curves.concepts.plato`,
    // owned by the curves package and not editable from this library-body pass.
    // Until it lands the `t.Turns` conversion is repeated in each `Eval` below.
    // See the matching note in the spirals section above.

    //==
    // # Shared helpers

    // The point at the given local coordinates of an orthonormal frame:
    // Origin + x*XAxis + y*YAxis + z*ZAxis. Places a curve written in its own
    // canonical position into world space.
    FramePoint(f: Frame3D, x: Number, y: Number, z: Number): Point3D
        => f.Origin + f.XAxis.Vector * x + f.YAxis.Vector * y + f.ZAxis.Vector * z;

    // The plane a frame's XY axes span: normal along Z, offset the projection
    // of the origin onto that normal.
    FramePlane(f: Frame3D): Plane
        => (f.ZAxis, f.ZAxis.Vector.Dot(f.Origin.PositionVector));

    //==
    // # Planar arcs in space

    // Every point of a circular arc lies in its frame's XY plane.
    CurvePlane(self: CircularArc3D): Plane
        => self.Frame.FramePlane;

    // The point at the swept angle on the circle of radius Radius in the
    // frame's XY plane.
    Eval(self: CircularArc3D, t: Number): Point3D
        => self.Frame.FramePoint(self.Radius * self.Angles.Lerp(t).Cos,
                                 self.Radius * self.Angles.Lerp(t).Sin,
                                 0.0);

    // Every point of an elliptical arc lies in its frame's XY plane.
    CurvePlane(self: EllipticalArc3D): Plane
        => self.Frame.FramePlane;

    // The point at the swept parametric angle on the ellipse with semi-axes
    // Radii along the frame's X and Y axes.
    Eval(self: EllipticalArc3D, t: Number): Point3D
        => self.Frame.FramePoint(self.Radii.X * self.Angles.Lerp(t).Cos,
                                 self.Radii.Y * self.Angles.Lerp(t).Sin,
                                 0.0);

    //==
    // # Polynomial arcs
    //
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B%C3%A9zier_curve
    // The Bernstein forms live in `library Polynomials` (polynomials.types.plato).

    // The quadratic Bezier point at t.
    Eval(self: QuadraticBezier3D, t: Number): Point3D
        => self.P0.PositionVector
               .QuadraticBezier(self.P1.PositionVector, self.P2.PositionVector, t)
               .ToPoint;

    // The cubic Bezier point at t.
    Eval(self: CubicBezier3D, t: Number): Point3D
        => self.P0.PositionVector
               .CubicBezier(self.P1.PositionVector, self.P2.PositionVector,
                            self.P3.PositionVector, t)
               .ToPoint;

    // The IDeformable3D obligation: every control point carried through the
    // mapping, with the same affine-exactness caveat as the plane arcs above.
    Deform(self: QuadraticBezier3D, mapping: Function1<Point3D, Point3D>): QuadraticBezier3D
        => (mapping(self.P0), mapping(self.P1), mapping(self.P2));
